questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose KI both because of the university's reputation as a leading medical university in europe, their course catalogue as well as because of the many nice things I have heard of Stockholm as a city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy both with accommodation through Karolinska as well as the contact with the Erasmus coordinator and information about courses!! All in all really nice and helpful so you can focus on being excited on going on exchange instead of stressing about these things.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I think usually there is offered a pickup by other students in the airport (a buddy system like in copenhagen) but because of COVID this was not possible. But we received a lot of guides on how to get from the airport to the accommodation on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think this is due to COVID, because usually there would be a buddy system and a tour around campus, but it was no problem since the campus in Solna is easy to find and figure out where to go for lectures etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were many options! there is a whole page full of different housing options. I went with the new Solna residence on campus which is a little more expensive but on campus so everything was in walking distance as well as the rooms and kitchen being completely new and big! Worth the extra money. You could choose to share kitchen on a floor (I chose this), shared apartments with 1 or 3 others or live by yourself with own kitchen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were different types of accommodation in the Solna residence - I chose studio with shared kitchen, where you have your own room and bathroom but share the kitchen with 15-20 other people! I loved it and you learn so many new people to know and about other cultures with people from all over the world.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is so worth it to be able to walk to class, and paying a little extra - my rent was still cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy - it is a part of the application for KI and their homepage is very easy to navigate

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: when you get a spot through Ucph, you need to apply to Karolinska directly. I received an email with all information, links and what i needed to fill out. It was very easy and clear.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You have the sweetest erasmus coordinator, Giulia, from Karolinska, who the danish coordinators put you in contact with and she is so nice and fast to reply and help with any question or anything you are in doubt about. I emailed her a lot both before and during my exchange and that was so nice.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very - I got the courses I applied to

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rather ask too much than too little - KI really wants to help you with any issue or question you may have

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose 3rd year on bachelor of Biomedicine at KI, so I followed two courses on 15 ECTS each. The level was good and not too hard. I would say the level was a little lower than copenhagen, but maybe that was just because you don't get grades - only pass or fail so you can relax a little more and on my courses the level of details needed for the exam was not as high as at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were mostly lectures, like in Copenhagen. But I missed the class room teaching a lot - like SAU or TØ. You only had lectures, but then there were also lab, maybe a few assignments and presentations which was nice to practice a little more since I haven't had that much oral presentations in UCPH. There were also a larger focus on the clinically parts of biomedicine which was interesting too.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Molecular Medicine - Oncology (15 points) 
Molecular Medicine - Cardiometabolic and infectious diseases (15 points)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked both of these courses and since they are on the same semester and year, you get to have classes with the same people throughout your stay (if you only plan to be there for 1 semester).
I chose KI because of oncology which was really interesting.

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really anything - you are covered by the EU card for health insurance (might need extra travel insurance so check that before). It seems that KI does not really use books or studying before lectures, so that was nice to not have to pay for it

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food is more expensive - both for going out for dinner and in the supermarkets (especially meat, chicken and fish). Alcohol is super expensive also both in systembolaget and out on bars and restaurants...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't really feel like there were that much - at least not offered or suitable for only one semester. There is a student union but you pay for a whole year.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The gym was free for students on campus, there were a few events for international students such as hikes or pub crawls you could sign up for that was nice. Also our erasmus coordinator was good to arrange dinners with all erasmus students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the KI global friends on facebook had many good events like hikes or bars etc so that was nice

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: we went to uppsala one day and Sigtuna another. We also took a cruise/ferry to helsinki as well as Tallinn, where you sleep on the boat and have a whole day in the destination before returning - really cheap and a good way to see places you haven't seen - i was very positively suprised by Tallinn in Estonia!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: At first the people in my class were a bit shy but after a week or two they opened up to us and that was nice! I spend most of my time with the 4 other exchange students on my courses as well as people from my housing that i met in the kitchen on the floor or through parties and other events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You can only buy alcohol in Systembolaget which closes super early in the weekend so this needs to be planned but other than that i didn't feel like there were that many differences from DK

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It was nice and easy to get used to since it was so like copenhagen and denmark

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) live in a housing with shared kitchen or in another way where you meet people!! I spend most time with other exchange students and people from my housing
2) Be prepared to use more money on food 
3) relax - the level is a little lower than in Cph but the courses are super interesting so just relax, enjoy your time and choose courses that fit your interests

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no i don't think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely the other people around me - i miss them so much already

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: always speaking english

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: nope

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
